items.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023
items.q: We had the band with Lou Marini, Alan Rubin, Howard Johnson, Paul Shaffer — we kind of started a trend.

ctx.x: Guess who I was speaking with an hour ago on the phone? Fred Lipsius.

Oh yes, oh my goodness, what a talented guy he is. Oh. He was the arranger for Blood, Sweat & Tears in the early days before I was in the band. And then my good friend of 56 © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
years Lou Marini took Fred’s place when he left the band, and went to be faculty at the Berklee School of Music.

items.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023
items.q: And then I’m looking out and I see my, you know Rubin and Howard Johnson and Cranshaw and the guys, Malone.

ctx.x: Okay. Do you get people, are you tired of people asking you about Steve Martin and King Tut?

No, no. Because you know that was such a crazy day. The guys were all treating me so weird, every time I walked in the dressing room they were tittering and I felt like I was interrupting something. They had bought a stink bomb which they were going to put in the sarcophagus and then they thought they’d all get fired. And then the make-up, they had to apply at like 6:30, they called me into make-up, and it was horrible. It was all my arms and shoulders and my chest and all over my face. It felt so constricting…
Boy, I guess so, with a capital C. Okay last question. Did your son, when did your son learn what a gig was?
